title: How much profit does the banana seller make?
description: A seller buys bananas by the kilogram and sells them one by one. The video finds the cost from the price of one kilogram, the sales from the price of one banana, and takes the cost away from the sales to get the profit.
teaching_notes: One idea: the amount for many is the price of one times how many, and profit is sales minus cost. Ask the class what money goes out and what money comes in before any work is shown. Watch for students who subtract the number of bananas from the number of kilograms.

source: End of chapter Figure it Out, Q3
video_script.why: The child can use the price of one unit to compare packs, and now uses the price of one unit to find a total, once for the cost and once for the sales.
video_script.substitution: The cost is the price of one kilogram times the kilograms, the sales are the price of one banana times the bananas, and the profit is the sales minus the cost.
video_script.anchor: A heap of bananas: 3 kg bought at 30 rupees per kg, 35 bananas in all, each banana sold for 5 rupees
video_script.payoff_line: The seller makes a profit of eighty five rupees
maths_rules: check: 175 is more than 90, so the seller gains, and 90 + 85 = 175
video_script.design: One idea: cost, then sales, then sales minus cost. The heap of bananas stays on the board all video; the working band builds in the idea part, one line for the cost, one for the sales and one for the profit.
open_questions: The book names the seller Shyamala; the name has no slot, so the video says the seller.

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='bought'/>A seller bought three kilograms of bananas at thirty rupees for each kilogram.
<bookmark mark='count'/>There were thirty five bananas in all.
<bookmark mark='sale'/>The seller sells each banana for five rupees.
How much profit does the seller make from selling all the bananas?

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: money out (cost) and money in (sales) shown as two stacks of coins; the words profit = sales − cost

marks.out: a stack of coins labelled cost, the money spent, appears
marks.in: a stack of coins labelled sales, the money received, appears
marks.rule: the words profit = sales − cost are written

narration: <bookmark mark='out'/>The money spent on the bananas is the cost.
<bookmark mark='in'/>The money received for the bananas is the sales.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>The profit is the sales minus the cost. Each total is the price of one, times how many.

beats.on_screen: Given: 3 kg bought at ₹30 per kg; 35 bananas; each banana sold for ₹5

marks.given: the three facts are written in the working band

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, three kilograms bought at thirty rupees for each kilogram. There are thirty five bananas, and each is sold for five rupees.

beats.on_screen: To find: the profit on selling all the bananas

marks.find: the find line is written under the given line

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the profit from selling all the bananas.

marks.why: the step title and the heap of bananas are lit

narration: <bookmark mark='why'/>Step one, find the cost of the bananas.
<bookmark mark='mult'/>Three kilograms at thirty rupees for each kilogram is three times thirty, which is ninety.
<bookmark mark='cost'/>The cost is ninety rupees.

marks.why: the step title and the sale tag are lit

narration: <bookmark mark='why'/>Step two, find the sales from the bananas.
<bookmark mark='mult'/>Thirty five bananas at five rupees each is thirty five times five. That is one hundred and seventy five.
<bookmark mark='sales'/>The sales are one hundred and seventy five rupees.

marks.sub: 175 − 90 is written with the two boxed amounts

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step three, the profit is the sales minus the cost.
<bookmark mark='sub'/>Take ninety away from one hundred and seventy five.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: check: 175 is more than 90, so there is a profit, not a loss

marks.gain: the word profit is lit and the word loss is crossed out

narration: <bookmark mark='cmp'/>Step four, check the answer makes sense.
<bookmark mark='gain'/>The sales are more than the cost, so the seller gains money. It is a profit, not a loss.

marks.tie: the cost and the sales are tied back to the profit

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The seller makes a profit of eighty five rupees.
<bookmark mark='tie'/>The cost was ninety rupees and the sales were one hundred and seventy five rupees.
